dimension_justifications.soundness: Within their stated assumptions, the displayed derivations appear coherent and deliberately avoid unsupported transfer to nonlinear SGD or unlearning. This review did not independently prove every result.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The scope, assumptions, proofs, and limitations are unusually explicit for a short theory paper, although the positioning does not make a distinct research contribution legible.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The three statements appear to be direct standard consequences of linear gradient dynamics, strong-convexity contraction, and conditional expectation. The submission does not identify a nonstandard theorem, object, or consequence that separates this collection from established elementary analysis.

paper_summary: The paper gives a fixed-quadratic matrix-product identity with a log-product remainder (T1), a clean-tail gradient-descent contraction bound under smooth strong convexity plus a conditional directional refinement (T2), and an affine scalar conditional-mean product identity (T3). It explicitly makes no empirical, deployment, nonlinear-SGD, or general unlearning claim.
strongest_verified_contribution: A carefully bounded and self-contained exposition that distinguishes fixed-quadratic, strongly convex clean-tail, and affine-recursion statements and explicitly rejects unsupported extrapolation among them.
strengths: The manuscript sharply limits its claims; source/paper.tex:21-33 and 241-260 explicitly rule out broad nonlinear, empirical, and deployment interpretations.
The T2 directional statement identifies the extra shared-invariant-subspace premise rather than treating a Rayleigh-quotient bound as sufficient (source/paper.tex:138-170).
The closest-work matrix does not claim empirical comparison or evidence that the snapshot does not contain (literature/closest_work_matrix.md:7-14).
questions: What exact mathematical statement or decision-relevant consequence is new relative to standard analyses of linear gradient descent, smooth strongly-convex gradient descent, and linear stochastic recursions? Please state it in one theorem-level sentence.
Which directly relevant optimization/theory results are the closest antecedents for T1, T2, and T3, and which assumption, conclusion, or proof obligation differs for each?
Can the authors formalize a nontrivial intervention-specific comparison between two training paths or objectives, rather than treating the clean-tail starting point w_s as arbitrary?

issues.location: source/paper.tex:77-120 (T1); source/paper.tex:125-175 (T2); source/paper.tex:180-213 (T3); source/paper.tex:46-51 (claimed three results)
issues.observed_evidence: T1 follows by iterating the linear gradient update and applying the Taylor-series bound for -log(1-x); T2 follows from the segment-average Hessian and the standard contraction norm bound; T3 follows by conditional and total expectation. The manuscript supplies no proposition showing that their combination yields a result unavailable from these standard arguments.
issues.why_it_matters: For a theory-only five-page paper, the theorem statements themselves must establish a clearly distinct conceptual or technical advance. Correctness and careful caveats do not alone make elementary special-case identities a publishable ICLR contribution.
issues.required_fix: Either add a precise, genuinely nontrivial intervention-specific theorem or consequence and prove it, or reframe the manuscript as a pedagogical/synthesis note and narrow claims of contribution accordingly. Explicitly state what aspect of each theorem is not implied by the closest prior theory.
issues.verification_test: An independent reader should be able to compare each revised main theorem with its named closest antecedent in a table of assumptions and conclusions, and identify at least one conclusion, regime, or proof difficulty not already covered; otherwise the manuscript must not present the results as a new research contribution.
issues.evidence_needed: Direct citations to closest optimization and stochastic-recursion theory plus a theorem-level novelty comparison; a new theorem requires a complete proof and clearly stated scope.

issues.observed_evidence: The related-work discussion and closest-work matrix primarily compare the paper to data-attribution, unlearning, noisy-label, and broad SGD-motivation papers. They contain no direct comparison to prior analyses of linear gradient-descent products, smooth strongly-convex gradient-descent convergence, or affine stochastic recursions, despite those being the paper's entire formal content.
issues.why_it_matters: The present comparisons establish that the paper is not an empirical attribution or unlearning method, but they do not establish novelty among the theory most likely to subsume T1--T3. Consequently, the novelty boundary cannot be assessed from the supplied citation record.
issues.required_fix: Replace or supplement the application-oriented related-work positioning with direct theoretical antecedents for each result. For each cited closest result, state whether it already proves the submitted statement, differs only in notation, or leaves a specifically identified gap filled here.
issues.verification_test: Check that every main theorem has at least one direct theoretical antecedent and an adjacent explicit comparison of assumptions and conclusion. If the authors cannot identify a substantive difference, the abstract, introduction, and contribution framing must call the result an exposition rather than a new theorem.
issues.evidence_needed: A citation-locked, theorem-level related-work comparison based on authoritative sources; broader literature completeness cannot be verified in this isolated no-browsing review.

issues.location: source/paper.tex:38-51 (problem framing); source/paper.tex:115-120 (T1 interpretation); source/paper.tex:173-175 (T2 interpretation); source/paper.tex:211-213 (T3 interpretation)
issues.observed_evidence: The motivating question concerns an objective changed along a training trajectory, but T2 conditions only on an arbitrary post-switch iterate w_s and T3 contains no intervention or comparison path. T1 provides a schedule product but no theorem comparing intervention versus clean trajectories. The shared product form therefore does not yet yield a formal result about the stated training-path intervention problem.
issues.why_it_matters: Without a theorem tying the results to an intervention-specific quantity, the paper's central framing risks being a relabeling of generic contraction facts. This further reduces significance even if all individual statements are correct.
issues.required_fix: Define an intervention-specific estimand involving two objectives or matched trajectories and prove a bound or impossibility result that uses the three-result framework; alternatively, revise the title, abstract, and introduction to present the work solely as bounded convex-dynamics preliminaries.
issues.verification_test: The revised paper should contain an explicit definition involving both the intervention and clean paths, followed by a theorem whose conclusion cannot be obtained by simply setting an arbitrary initial point in standard clean-objective contraction. If absent, verify that intervention/unlearning framing is removed from headline claims.
issues.evidence_needed: A formal comparison theorem with proof, or claim-narrowing edits consistent across title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion.

ethics_concerns: No active empirical or deployment claim is made. The manuscript appropriately notes that any future human-label experiment must address data permissions and forbidden decision-time information (source/paper.tex:270-275).
llm_usage_disclosure: This is an isolated GPT-5.6 Terra subagent review for internal presubmission QA.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A theorem-level comparison to direct prior theory demonstrating a substantive, previously unproved intervention-specific result.
A rigorous new result connecting matched intervention and clean trajectories under assumptions that materially extend standard contraction or affine-recursion analysis.
Consistent claim narrowing that accurately represents the work as a useful but limited synthesis; this could improve clarity but would not alone establish accept-level novelty.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Direct prior theory showing that any of T1--T3 already appears under equivalent assumptions and conclusions.
A counterexample to the stated directional invariant-subspace conclusion or another proof error.
Revision text that restores empirical, unlearning, or nonlinear-SGD implications without corresponding evidence.
review_limitations: This was an isolated snapshot-only review; no web browsing or literature search was performed, so broader related-work completeness cannot be independently verified.
The assessment emphasizes novelty and positioning; it is not a substitute for a line-by-line independent proof audit.
